Name: Talisman's South Park ontology explainer
Description: Jessica Talisman's South Park Ontology Explainer, as a rulebook: the page's ten facts, five rule switches, property wiring, provenance wording and current-value policy are rows, and every conclusion is a formula. The rules apply in three fixed strata (inverse and symmetric, then the property chain, then domain and range); property wiring that feeds an earlier stratum would need repeated rounds. Every fact that could hold over the cast is a candidate row; app/lib/candidates.mjs writes the candidates when a thing, value or property is added.

schema.name: CountOfTypeFirings

schema.name: Holds
schema.Description: Order 15. TRUE when in effect or concluded by an enabled rule; the graph draws it. Blank when nothing states or concludes it: not known, never FALSE (open world: removing a statement does not say that its opposite is true).

schema.name: IsConclusion
schema.Description: Order 16. TRUE when the fact holds only because a rule concluded it; drawn dashed. Blank otherwise: a stated fact is not a conclusion, and a fact nothing concludes is not known (never FALSE).

schema.name: HoldsUnit
schema.Description: Order 16. 1 when the fact holds.

schema.name: ConclusionUnit
schema.Description: Order 17. 1 when the fact is a conclusion.

schema.name: ParentUnit
schema.Description: Order 16. 1 for a holding parent link.

schema.name: GrandparentUnit
schema.Description: Order 16. 1 for a holding grandparent link.

schema.name: PlaceUnit
schema.Description: Order 16. 1 for a holding attends link.

schema.name: FirstPreChainOrderKey
schema.Description: Order 7. Order key of the first inverse or symmetric application that concludes this fact.

schema.name: SnapPosition
schema.Description: Order 8. Where the page's reasoner meets this fact as a premise: a stated fact at its list position, a fact concluded by the inverse or symmetric rule after every stated fact, in the order it was concluded; 0 for a fact that does not hold yet, so a link to no fact reads the same on every engine.

schema.name: FirstFiredOrderKey
schema.Description: Order 15. Order key of the first rule application that concludes this fact, in the page reasoner's order.

schema.name: CountOfChosenFirings

schema.name: SubjectNodeKey
schema.Description: Order 1. The graph node this fact starts from.

schema.name: ObjectNodeKey
schema.Description: Order 2. The graph node this fact points at: the thing, or one node per value and datatype.

schema.name: SubjectNodeKind
schema.Description: Order 19. How the graph draws the subject.

schema.name: ObjectThingNodeKind
schema.Description: Order 19. How the graph draws the object thing.

schema.name: ObjectNodeKind
schema.Description: Order 20. How the graph draws the object: a value, a class, a place or a person.

schema.name: ObjectValueNodeLabel
schema.Description: Order 1. The small label under a value node.

schema.name: CountOfViolationsAsFirst
schema.Description: Order 18. Violated disjointness checks naming this fact first.

schema.name: CountOfViolationsAsSecond
schema.Description: Order 18. Violated disjointness checks naming this fact second.

schema.name: IsInContradiction
schema.Description: Order 19. Part of a contradiction the disjoint rule found; drawn in the alarm colour.

data.Text: South Park Ontology Explainer, on one rulebook
data.Name: page-title

data.Text: A rulebook rebuild of the explainer by
data.Name: byline-prefix

data.Text: South Park facts form a knowledge graph
data.Name: title

data.Text: An ontology defines kinds of things, their properties and rules. This knowledge graph uses those definitions to connect facts about South Park. Stan’s school facts can change while Stan stays the same person.
data.Name: intro

data.Text: This version runs no reasoner in the browser. Every fact, rule switch and conclusion on the page is a row or a formula in one rulebook, and the engine you pick below computes it: Postgres views, generated TypeScript, or the generated OWL and SHACL rules.
data.Name: intro-rulebook

data.Text: Drag a circle to move it. Tap a circle or a line to read its facts and sources.
data.Name: key-help

data.Text: Character portraits and South Park Elementary are Fandom images, linked from the rulebook’s Things table. Dashed circles mark classes; solid circles show individual things or values.
data.Name: image-note

data.Text: Each statement has three parts, called a triple. The subject identifies what we describe. The predicate tells how it is connected to the object. The object is the related thing or value. Select a fact to show it.
data.Name: statements-hint

data.Text: Stan can change while his identity stays the same
data.Name: scenario-heading

data.Text: The grade-5 and leaving-school buttons imagine future changes so you can see how the model responds. They do not report events from the show. Stan is allowed to graduate. The database does not get a vote.
data.Name: scenario-hint

data.Text: Rules add facts to the graph
data.Name: rules-heading

data.Text: An inference is a new conclusion from facts and a rule. Reasoning means following rules step by step to reach or check conclusions. Here the rulebook does that work: each rule is a switch, and every conclusion is a formula.
data.Name: rules-hint

data.Text: Try Sharon, is parent of, Stan. Then try Sharon, is parent of, Randy with the disjoint rule on.
data.Name: add-hint

data.Text: For has grade level, enter an integer (a number with no fractional part), such as 4 or 5. This form checks integer input as an application check. For has role, enter text such as Student. A new grade or role replaces that person’s previous active value in this page’s current record. Uncheck a role fact to clear it.
data.Name: grade-input-note

data.Name: integer-error
